newsitem.title: CHINA: HK property stocks dive as interbank rates rise.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks dive as interbank rates rise.

text.p: Property stocks were hit hard by Tuesday's tumble in Hong Kong share prices with investors fearing higher mortgage lending rates as interbank rates surged amid fears about a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar.
Shares in Cheung Kong tumbled HK$3.25 to HK$88.75 and Henderson Land fell HK$2.50 to HK$67.75. Sun Hung Kai Properties was down HK$2.50 at HK$93.75.

"The property sector is under huge sellng pressure. Interbank rates are increasing so banks might increase their mortgage rates again," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.

"A quarter point rise in interest rates won't hurt too much but investors fear that if banks increase rates over the longer term, it will keep the speculative interest out of the market and property prices will remain at a lower level," said Tam.
Benjamin Cheng, executive director at Goldman Sachs, said investors had already discounted the downward pressure on property prices going forward.

"The property market has actually fallen quite a lot. I don't see the sector underperforming from this point but there is probably some short-term downside. People will definitely get more realistic," he said.
Goldman has an overweight position on property stocks and is likely to maintain that, Cheng said.
Yamaichi International analyst Philip Chan said interbank rates could cool over coming days if concerns about the Hong Kong dollar fade, allowing banks to avoid an increase in mortgage lending rates.

"Speculators will not find it as easy to attack the Hong Kong dollar as other currencies in the region. Hong Kong has very strong foreign reserves and China may give a hand to the Hong Kong government if the Hong Kong currency is really under attack," he said. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
